newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chernomyrdin says new reform govt nearly ready.
newsitem.headline: Chernomyrdin says new reform govt nearly ready.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Saturday that a major overhaul of his government, bringing in new faces and taking a radical new approach to economic form, was nearly ready.

"We are finishing our work on the structure," Chernomyrdin told ORT Television in an interview. He added that changes had been in progress since December. Reforms would be unpopular but had to be pushed through by a decisive, united team, he said.
Chernomyrdin, who was charged with shaking up the government by President Boris Yeltsin a week ago, said he had realised last November that the economy was "going nowhere".

Now the whole structure of the administration would change in order to push ahead with economic reforms under the guidance of Anatoly Chubais, who was appointed Chernomyrdin's first deputy by Yeltsin.
Some ministries covering industrial sectors which had now been largely privatised would be sharply cut back or scrapped, Chernomyrdin said.
"There will be unpopular decisions, but we have to do it," he added. "We cannot drag out the process of reform, we cannot drag out people's suffering."
Chernomyrdin gave no indication when the changes would be announced but noted that the process of choosing personnel had not been easy.
The Kremlin says the new government should be unveiled on Monday or Tuesday.
